title: the Vijnana Bhairava (112 practices, one a day for 40 days)
hook: a packed bus home, and the same knowing in every seat
carry: the Vijnana Bhairava (112 practices, one a day for 40 days)
tomorrow: your mind wanders off mid-sit. where exactly did it go?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Vijnana Bhairava caught a want at its first flicker and let it settle back where it came from. Today, the book looks up from the cushion, at everyone else.

The last bus home, packed to the doors. A nurse still in scrubs, asleep against the window. Two kids sharing one pair of earbuds. A man on the phone saying I know, I know, to someone who can't see him nod. Nobody looks at anybody. Each person is a whole world, sealed shut, riding the same bus. And a question floats up somewhere between stops: is the seeing behind each pair of eyes as private as it feels? The Vijnana Bhairava has a verse with an answer, and it's not the one the bus would suggest.
screen: `THE LAST BUS HOME.` → `EVERYONE SEALED IN.` → `HOW PRIVATE IS SEEING?`

segments.voice: Here's the verse, in plain words. The awareness of knower and known, someone seeing something, is common to everyone who has a body. What sets the practiced apart, Bhairava says, is attention to it. They notice the knowing itself; everyone else looks straight through it to the thing that's known. So the nurse, the kids, the man on the phone are each lit by the same kind of knowing. Not similar lamps in separate boxes. The same plain fact, in every seat. A neighboring verse goes further. A wanting, a knowing, the awareness of something as ordinary as a clay pot: these don't arise only in me, it says. They arise in others too. Hold that steadily, and a person becomes as wide as everything. Notice the turn this run has taken. The breath, the fading sound, the sneeze, the first flicker of a want all happened inside one person. This door opens outward. The knowing that rests at the turn of my breath is also shining in the stranger across the aisle, who will never learn my name. In the book's terms, seeing that is one more door to Bhairava. And here's the line worth repeating at dinner: on this reading, the plainest thing anyone has, simply being aware, is the very thing every person shares.
screen: `KNOWER AND KNOWN, IN EVERY BODY.` · `THE PRACTICED NOTICE THE KNOWING.` · `NOT ONLY IN ME: IN OTHERS TOO.` · `THE DOOR OPENS OUTWARD.` · then, large: `THE SAME KNOWING IN EVERY SEAT.`

segments.voice: Listen for the farthest sound you can hear: traffic, a fan, a voice through a wall. Somewhere near that sound, someone else is hearing too. Rest in your own hearing, and let it sink in that the same plain knowing is lit in them right now.
The Vijnana Bhairava: a tantric book of doors. Today's door is the knowing that's lit in everyone who has a body.
For the road: the Vijnana Bhairava, and the same knowing in every seat on the bus. Day sixteen twenty-five.
